assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md 'Epic Hierarchy' section specifies 'Grouping strategy: by-repository' and lists two Epics: 'Epic 1 | TC-9006: trustify-backend | Epic (level 1) | TC-9006' and 'Epic 2 | TC-9006: trustify-ui | Epic (level 1) | TC-9006'. Both Epics sit between the Feature (TC-9006) and the 11 Tasks in the Task-to-Epic Assignment table.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epic Hierarchy table shows Epic 1 summary as 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and Epic 2 summary as 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Both exactly match the prescribed format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>'.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Task-to-Epic Assignment table: Tasks 2, 3, 4 (Repository: trustify-backend in their task files) are assigned to Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-backend'. Tasks 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 (Repository: trustify-ui in their task files) are assigned to Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Cross-verified each task file's '## Repository' section against the impact-map assignment — all are consistent.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md 'Issue Links' section contains 'Feature to Epics (Incorporates)' subsection: 'TC-9006 Incorporates Epic 1 (TC-9006: trustify-backend)' and 'TC-9006 Incorporates Epic 2 (TC-9006: trustify-ui)'. Line 45 explicitly states: 'Feature "Incorporates" links go from TC-9006 to each Epic (not to individual Tasks).' No Feature-to-Task Incorporates links appear anywhere.

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks are numbered 2, 3, 4; frontend tasks are numbered 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. Cross-epic dependency: Task 5 (frontend) depends on Task 3 (backend). Within backend: Task 3 depends on Task 2, Task 4 depends on Task 3. Within frontend: Task 6 depends on Task 5, Task 7 depends on Task 6, Task 8 depends on Task 7, Task 9 depends on Tasks 7 and 8. All dependency arrows point from lower-numbered to higher-numbered tasks.

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Task 1 (task-1-create-feature-branch.md) and Task 11 (task-11-merge-feature-branch.md) are bookend tasks that are neither documentation nor testing tasks. Both lack 'Files to Modify', 'Files to Create', and 'Implementation Notes' sections. Task 1 has only: Repository, Target Branch, Bookend Type, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements, Dependencies. Task 11 has only: Repository, Target Branch, Bookend Type, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements, Dependencies. The assertion only exempts documentation and testing tasks, not bookend tasks. All other non-exempt tasks (2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8) contain all required sections.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md 'Epic Creation Details' section shows two jira.create_issue calls, both with issueTypeName='Epic' and parent='TC-9006'. The Epic Hierarchy table confirms 'Epic (level 1)' as the Issue Type and 'TC-9006' as the Parent for both Epics.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 11 task files contain a '## Repository' section with a single repository name: Tasks 2, 3, 4 specify 'trustify-backend'; Tasks 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 specify 'trustify-ui'. No task lists multiple repositories.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 11 task files contain '## Target Branch', '## Description', '## Acceptance Criteria', and '## Test Requirements' sections. Verified in each file: task-1 (main), task-2 through task-9 (TC-9006), task-10 (TC-9006), task-11 (main). Each section contains substantive content, not just headers.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:', not a placeholder, abbreviated value, or example string
assertion_results.evidence: All 11 digest files exist (task-1-digest.md through task-11-digest.md). Each contains '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-hex-chars>'. Examples: task-1-digest.md has 'sha256-md:3e5829262a268653232106145ebba643a9be270c8829d188c53df4e7cd187fb1', task-2-digest.md has 'sha256-md:8d04f016bc52337a0267eda3655f2a95c9c253f9dd4899d90a2120e751b37912'. All hashes are exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, not placeholders or abbreviated values.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention rationales in Implementation Notes follow the prescribed format. Backend tasks (2-4) include only Rust-scoped conventions with rationales like 'Applies: task creates modules/fundamental/src/remediation/model/summary.rs matching the convention's Rust module structure scope' (task-2). Frontend tasks (5-9) include only TypeScript/React-scoped conventions with rationales like 'Applies: task modifies src/api/models.ts matching the convention's TypeScript file scope' (task-5). No 'Not applicable' annotations appear in any task file. No cross-scope contamination: backend tasks do not include TypeScript conventions and vice versa. All rationales name specific files from Files to Modify or Files to Create.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9006 has Priority: Major (from feature-epic-hierarchy.md). impact-map.md 'Inherited Field Values' states: 'Priority: Major (inherited from TC-9006, propagated to all Epics and Tasks)'. Epic Creation Details include 'priority: {"name": "Major"}' in additional_fields for both Epics. summary-comment.md 'Inherited Field Propagation' section confirms: 'Priority: Major -- inherited from TC-9006 and propagated to all created Epics and Tasks via additional_fields.priority.name'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9006 has fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (from feature-epic-hierarchy.md). CLAUDE.md has no '### Jira Field Defaults' section, so fixVersion scope defaults to 'both'. impact-map.md 'Inherited Field Values' states: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (inherited from TC-9006, propagated to all Epics and Tasks; no fixVersion scope configured in Jira Field Defaults, defaulting to "both")'. Epic Creation Details include 'fixVersions: [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]' in additional_fields for both Epics. summary-comment.md confirms propagation with scope default explanation.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains an 'Inherited Field Propagation' section documenting: 'Priority: Major -- inherited from TC-9006 and propagated to all created Epics and Tasks' and 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 -- inherited from TC-9006 and propagated to all created Epics and Tasks'. Additionally, impact-map.md contains an 'Inherited Field Values' section with the same information. The 'additional_fields applied to all created issues' JSON block in summary-comment.md shows the exact field values: {"labels": ["ai-generated-jira"], "priority": {"name": "Major"}, "fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]}.
